attack.reason: A certificate blacklist match is threat-intelligence context rather than direct evidence of one ATT&CK behavior or technique.

detections.behavior: Matches a TLS server certificate SHA-1 fingerprint against the reviewed SSLBL snapshot updated 2026-08-05T13:09:49.000Z; the source is build-expired after seven days.
limitations: Certificate reuse, shared infrastructure, source errors, or post-listing remediation can produce false positives; validate current context before response.

Detection requires a visible TLS server certificate on any destination port in a complete captured handshake; TLS resumption, packet loss, asymmetric capture, or midstream starts can prevent inspection.
Only the certificate SHA-1 fingerprint is compared; encrypted application payloads and endpoint behavior are not inspected.
The reviewed SSLBL snapshot expires at 2026-08-12T13:09:49.000Z and a stale source blocks pack build and signing.
nonClaims: Does not prove endpoint compromise, malicious payload delivery, or ownership of an observed public or private address.
The indicator match does not authorize automatic blocking; human review is required.
detections.title: SSLBL malicious TLS certificate fingerprint
